title: August TV Is Stacked: The Shards, Ted Lasso, Lanterns and More Hit Screens
excerpt: From Ryan Murphy's serial-killer thriller to the DC Universe's prestige debut featuring Poorna Jagannathan, August 2026 brings an unusually loaded slate of premieres across every major streamer.
body:
• August 5 alone brings The Shards (FX/Hulu), Ted Lasso Season 4 (Apple TV), One Hundred Years of Solitude Part 2 (Netflix), and Sterling Point (Prime Video)
  • Indian-origin actress Poorna Jagannathan plays a key role in HBO's Lanterns, the DC Universe's prestige debut premiering August 16
  • Later in the month, Reacher returns for Season 4, It's Always Sunny hits Season 18, and FX comedy Adults gets a sophomore run

American television rarely packs this much firepower into a single month, but August 2026 is shaping up as one of the most competitive stretches in recent streaming history. On August 5 alone, four high-profile series launch across four different platforms — and that's before HBO drops its most anticipated superhero project of the year later in the month.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Zpm9HUOrZIc

A Blockbuster First Week

The biggest debut of the month may be The Shards, Ryan Murphy's nine-episode adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's semi-autobiographical 2023 novel. Set in 1981 Los Angeles, the FX series follows a 17-year-old version of Ellis (played by Igby Rigney) at the elite Buckley School, where the arrival of a magnetic new student, Robert Mallory (Homer Gere, son of Richard Gere), coincides with a serial killer called The Trawler terrorizing the city. Evan Rachel Wood, Wes Bentley, and Kaia Gerber round out a cast that screams prestige horror. The series premieres August 5 at 9 p.m. ET on FX and Hulu.

The same day, Ted Lasso returns for a long-awaited Season 4 on Apple TV+. Jason Sudeikis is back as the eternally optimistic coach, this time leading a second-division women's football team in Richmond. Hannah Waddingham, Juno Temple, and Jeremy Swift return alongside new additions including Tanya Reynolds, Faye Marsay, and Jude Mack.

Netflix counters with the finale of One Hundred Years of Solitude, dropping Part 2 of its acclaimed adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez's masterwork on August 5. The eight-episode second season, filmed entirely in Colombia with local actors, picks up after the armistice and treaty of Neerlandia as the Buendía family faces new upheaval. A second batch of episodes follows on August 26, bringing the 16-episode series to a close. Prime Video also enters the fray with Sterling Point, a YA mystery from Megan Park backed by Josh Schwartz and Stephanie Savage, the producers behind The O.C. and Gossip Girl.

Lanterns Brings DC to Prestige TV

On August 16, HBO debuts Lanterns, the first live-action series in James Gunn's rebooted DC Universe and arguably the month's most ambitious swing. Created by Chris Mundy (Ozark), Damon Lindelof (Watchmen), and comic-book writer Tom King, the eight-episode series pairs veteran Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) with rookie recruit John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) as they investigate a murder in small-town Nebraska.

"This is the first script that I've read that I understand why there's an NDA. It is the best writing that I have ever read."

— Poorna Jagannathan, actress (Lanterns)

The supporting cast is stacked: Kelly Macdonald plays the local sheriff, Ulrich Thomsen is classic villain Sinestro, Nathan Fillion reprises his Superman role as Guy Gardner, and Laura Linney has joined in an undisclosed part. Mundy has described the series as "as much of a buddy cop show as a superhero show," drawing comparisons to True Detective.
nri_angle: Poorna Jagannathan, the Indian-origin Never Have I Ever star, plays a key recurring role in HBO's Lanterns, one of the month's biggest premieres, marking growing South Asian visibility in superhero tentpoles.
